# peak-media decisions log

IDs are stable. A decision is changed by adding a new entry that supersedes it, never by editing the old one. Contract changes use the ADDED / MODIFIED / REMOVED form in the **Contract changes** section (orchestration §7).

## Contract changes

*None yet. Format:*

```
### CC-NN — <contract> v<N> — <date> — requested by <WP>
ADDED:    <field> — <reason>
MODIFIED: <field> — <old> → <new> — <reason>
REMOVED:  <field> — <reason>
Decision: accepted | rejected — schemaVersion bump? yes/no
```

## Run-time findings

*Facts learned during the build that later WPs depend on (e.g. the PCM sample rate from AC-TTS-07).*

- **2026-11-08 (F1 end-to-end, British-accent experiment — abandoned by the user):** Rasalgethi with "Speak with a British accent" in the style held the accent on short clips but dropped it on the 28-word compare clip in every variant (accent last, accent in every mood tag, accent first, no tag, accent-only tag). Style-instructed accents aren't reliable; use a natively accented voice if one is needed.
- **2026-11-08 (WP3a, AC-TTS-07 live run by the Lead):** OpenRouter `/api/v1/audio/speech` returns **24 kHz mono PCM** for both `google/gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts` (Achird, 177 wpm, −19.3 LUFS) and `microsoft/mai-voice-2.1-flash` (en-GB-Emily, 161 wpm, −16.8 LUFS). Each request carried `"provider":{"zdr":true}`; Gemini with ZDR was accepted on this account. The key was redacted in both debug logs (0 leaks).
- **2026-11-08 (WP2):** HyperFrames 0.9.25 renders correctly here, so the DEC-05 fallback to 0.9.23 is not needed. A 3 s 1280×720 plate takes about 7 s; two renders give identical `framemd5`, and a render with outbound network blocked (macOS `sandbox-exec`, loopback allowed) matches the online one.
- **HF composition rules found in WP2:** elements with class `clip` are positioned absolutely by the runtime, so a flex layout needs one `clip` wrapper around its children. Timelines register via `window.__timelines["main"]`. GSAP is loaded from a local `vendor/gsap.min.js` (the HF scaffold defaults to a CDN URL, which we never use).
- **Template placeholders** must not appear inside HTML comments (the WP2 F0 sheet caught `{{LINES}}` being substituted into a comment).
- **2026-11-10 (WP11, U1 — YouTube upload settings, page read 2026-11-10):** support.google.com/youtube/answer/1722171 gives MP4 with fast start and no edit lists; H.264 High, progressive, 2 consecutive B-frames, closed GOP of half the frame rate, CABAC, VBR, 4:2:0; AAC-LC 48 kHz stereo 384 kbps; SDR 1080p 8 Mbps at 24–30 fps, 12 Mbps at 48–60 fps. **Matches plan §4.6 `youtube` on every value.** WP13: encode it as written, keep CABAC (x264 High default) and write no edit lists. Evidence: `evidence/WP11/U1-youtube-settings.log`.
- **2026-11-10 (WP11, U2 — screencast 1920×1080 @ 60 fps): PASS.** Two 30 s headless takes of a continuous-motion page with the `browserPath()` headless shell (Chrome 152), counted like `FrameGrid`: 1798/1800 slots fresh (99.9 %, 59.9 unique fps) and 1775/1800 (98.6 %, 59.2 unique fps), max frame gap 18–19 ms. WP13: `hifi` may capture at 60 fps; no fallback needed. Evidence: `evidence/WP11/U2-screencast-1080p60.json`.
- **2026-11-10 (WP11, U3 — cursor via `screencast.showOverlay`): PASS.** A 1200 px, 400 ms glide showed 12–13 distinct positions at 30 fps and 24–25 at 60 fps (every slot new), whether by re-issuing the overlay each step (~600 dispose+show calls per glide; not rate-limited) or by **one** overlay whose HTML carries a CSS keyframe glide. The overlay survives `page.goto` and `reload` and is removed by dispose. Playwright's own `showActions({ cursor: 'pointer' })` also glides (16–18 positions at 60 fps) but owns the timing. WP12: draw the cursor with `showOverlay`, one overlay per glide with a CSS animation; no DOM re-injection after navigation. Evidence: `evidence/WP11/U3-overlay-cursor.json`.
- **2026-11-10 (WP11, U4 — `storageState()` after the last tab closes): PASS.** Headed, Playwright 1.65.0, both `launch()+newContext()` and `launchPersistentContext()`: after `page.close()` or a browser-side close (CDP `Target.closeTarget`, the tab-× path) the page `close` event fires within ~5 ms, the context and browser stay up, and `storageState()` returns the HttpOnly cookie, the JS cookie and the localStorage entry. A real mouse click on the tab × was not performed (it would drive the user's screen). `window.close()` from the page is ignored for a tab the script didn't open. WP14: `signin` waits for the last page's `close` event, then reads `storageState()`; keep the `!`-keypress fallback only as a timeout escape. Evidence: `evidence/WP11/U4-storage-after-close.json`.
- **2026-11-10 (WP11, U5 — screencast with `headless: false`): PASS.** 5 s headed takes delivered frames normally: Playwright's Chrome for Testing 158 at 30 fps 96 % (28.8 unique fps), at 60 fps 99.7 % (59.8); Google Chrome 157 (`channel: 'chrome'`) at 30 fps 96.7 %. WP14: `--headed` can record, **provided a headed-capable browser exists (see U6)**. Evidence: `evidence/WP11/U5-headed-screencast.json`.
- **2026-11-10 (WP11, U6 — headed Chromium from what `setup.sh` installs): FAIL — no written fallback; Lead decision needed.** `browserPath()` returns HyperFrames' `chrome-headless-shell` 152, which accepts `headless: false` but stays headless (UA `HeadlessChrome`, no window); `setup.sh` installs nothing else (`npm ci --ignore-scripts`, then `hyperframes browser ensure`). Headed works on this Mac only via browsers setup didn't install: Playwright's `chromium-1254` in `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright` (left by an unrelated project on 2026-11-09) and the user's `/Applications/Google Chrome.app` (`channel: 'chrome'`). Options for the Lead: (a) `signin`/`--headed` use `channel: 'chrome'` and stop with one line when Chrome is absent; (b) setup downloads Playwright's Chromium (376 MB on disk here; the brief forbids adding it here); (c) both, Chrome first. WP14 is blocked on this choice. Evidence: `evidence/WP11/U6-headed-launch.log`.
